name: Abū ʿUthmān Bakr ibn Muḥammad al-Māzinī
summary: Basran master of the generation after Sībawayh's students, author of al-Taṣrīf, the oldest book on ṣarf that survives, and teacher of al-Mubarrad.
bio: Al-Māzinī read al-Kitāb with al-Akhfash and learnt from al-Aṣmaʿī and Abū ʿUbayda; al-Zubaydī puts him first in the seventh Basran generation. Al-Mubarrad was his student, and through al-Mubarrad his teaching reached the Baghdad of the next century.

His Kitāb al-Taṣrīf is the first book given wholly to ṣarf that has come down to us: the patterns, augmentation, the weak letters and their changes. Ibn Jinnī wrote a commentary on it, al-Munṣif, and the two together became the classical treatment of the subject before Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Shāfiya.

The biographers (Yāqūt and Ibn Khallikān among them) tell a story of reward. A non-Muslim offered him a hundred dinars to read Sībawayh's book with him, and al-Māzinī refused, since the book quotes the Qurʾān. Soon after, a slave-girl sang before the caliph al-Wāthiq the line 'O wronging one, your striking down a man (rajulan) who greeted you…', and was corrected to rajulun; she held to rajulan and named al-Māzinī as her teacher. He was summoned to Samarra, explained why rajulan is right, the object of the maṣdar muṣābakum, and went home with a thousand dinars. He died in Basra in 249/863.

works.title: Kitāb al-Taṣrīf
works.note: The oldest surviving book on ṣarf; commented on by Ibn Jinnī in al-Munṣif.

uncertain: His death is also given as 248/862.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 30 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
